name: clarify-requirements
description: Turns a vague request into a short, testable spec. Use at the start of any task whose goal, inputs, outputs or limits are not clear.
must: restate the goal in one sentence
list inputs, outputs, constraints, non-goals
write 3-6 acceptance criteria as checkable statements
list open questions; ask the user only the ones that change the work
no code at this step

name: break-down-work
description: Splits a feature or project into small, ordered tasks that each end in something testable. Use before starting work that takes more than an hour.
must: each task: one outcome, how to verify it, rough size
order by dependency and risk; riskiest unknown first
a walking skeleton end-to-end before polishing
mark what can be done in parallel
keep tasks under half a day

name: estimate-and-risks
description: Gives an honest estimate with ranges and the risks behind it. Use when asked how long something takes or whether it is feasible.
must: estimate as a range (best, likely, worst) with assumptions
name the top risks and what would reduce each
separate known work from research
say what would change the estimate

name: design-architecture
description: Designs the structure of a system or component: parts, responsibilities, data flow, interfaces. Use for new systems or large changes.
must: start from requirements and constraints (load, latency, data size, team)
propose 2 options with trade-offs, recommend one
components and their single responsibility
data flow and where state lives
failure modes and how each is handled
a mermaid diagram when it helps

name: write-adr
description: Records an architecture decision as an ADR. Use when a technical choice is made that others will later ask about.
must: format: title, status, context, decision, alternatives considered, consequences
consequences include the downsides
short: one page
date and who decided

name: design-api
description: Designs an HTTP or library API: endpoints or functions, inputs, outputs, errors, versioning. Use before implementing a public interface.
must: resource and method naming conventions (REST) or function signatures
request and response examples
error model with status codes and messages
pagination, idempotency, versioning
validation rules at the boundary
OpenAPI or type signatures as the contract

name: model-data
description: Designs a database schema or data model. Use when adding tables, collections or persistent formats.
must: entities, keys, relations, cardinality
normalise first, denormalise only for a measured need
constraints in the database (not null, unique, foreign keys, checks)
indexes for the real queries
how the schema will be migrated
sample queries for the main use cases

name: implement-feature
description: Implements a feature in an existing codebase, end to end, with tests. Use for any new behaviour.
must: read the surrounding code and follow its patterns
smallest change that delivers the acceptance criteria
tests for the new behaviour, written with or before the code
handle errors at boundaries; no silent failures
run the tests and linters before saying done
summarise what changed and how it was checked

name: write-python
description: Writes idiomatic, typed, testable Python. Use whenever writing Python code.
must: Python 3.11+, type hints, from __future__ import annotations
standard library first; pathlib, dataclasses, logging
small functions, clear names, no global state
specific exceptions; never bare except
ruff and mypy --strict clean
docstrings that say what, not how

name: write-go
description: Writes idiomatic Go. Use whenever writing Go code.
must: gofmt, go vet, errors returned not panicked
wrap errors with context (fmt.Errorf %w)
small interfaces defined by the consumer
context.Context first argument for I/O
table-driven tests, -race
no global mutable state; constructor functions

name: write-typescript
description: Writes safe, typed TypeScript for Node or the browser. Use whenever writing TypeScript or JavaScript.
must: strict mode, no any; unknown at boundaries and narrow it
validate external input (zod or hand checks)
async/await with error handling; no floating promises
small modules, named exports
tests with the project's runner (vitest/jest/node:test)

name: write-sql
description: Writes correct, safe and efficient SQL and migrations. Use for queries, schema changes and data fixes.
must: parameterised queries only; never string-built SQL
explain the plan for slow or large queries; use indexes
migrations are reversible and safe on a live table (add nullable, backfill, then constrain)
transactions for multi-statement changes
test on a copy before production data

name: write-cli
description: Builds a command-line tool that is pleasant for people and scripts. Use when creating a CLI.
must: argparse/click/cobra with --help that explains each option
exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 usage
--json output for scripts; human text by default
errors to stderr with a fix hint
no interactive prompts when not a TTY
tests that call main() with arguments

name: concurrency
description: Writes correct concurrent or asynchronous code. Use for threads, async, parallel jobs, queues or shared state.
must: prefer message passing or immutable data over shared state
every lock has a clear owner; no I/O while holding a lock
timeouts and cancellation on every wait
bounded queues and back-pressure
test with races in mind (-race, many runs)

name: algorithms
description: Chooses and implements the right algorithm and data structure. Use for performance-sensitive logic or interview-style problems.
must: state input size and the needed complexity first
pick data structures for the operations needed
explain time and space complexity
handle edge cases: empty, one, duplicates, huge
test against a brute-force version on random inputs

name: write-tests
description: Writes useful automated tests. Use when adding behaviour, fixing a bug or covering untested code.
must: one behaviour per test; name says the behaviour
arrange, act, assert; result in got
edge cases and error paths
no network, clock or real files in unit tests; fakes at the boundary
integration tests for the main paths
never weaken a test to make it pass

name: debug
description: Finds the root cause of a bug methodically. Use for errors, crashes, wrong results or flaky behaviour.
must: reproduce first, with the smallest input
read the full error and stack trace
form one hypothesis at a time and test it (logs, debugger, bisect)
find the root cause, not the symptom
write a failing test, then fix, then show it passing
note what else the cause may affect

name: review-code
description: Reviews a change for bugs and risks. Use for pull requests, diffs or code the user asks you to check.
must: correctness first: logic, edge cases, error handling
security: input validation, secrets, injection
tests: are changed behaviours covered
each finding: file:line, the concrete input that breaks it, the fix
most serious first; no style nitpicks unless they hide a bug
say clearly when nothing is wrong

name: refactor
description: Improves code structure without changing behaviour. Use when code is hard to change or read.
must: tests pass before starting; add characterisation tests if missing
small steps, each keeping tests green
one kind of change per commit (rename, extract, move)
no behaviour change mixed in
stop when the target change becomes easy

name: performance
description: Makes code faster or lighter based on measurement. Use when something is slow or uses too much memory.
must: measure first: profile, benchmark, numbers before and after
find the bottleneck; do not guess
fix the algorithm before micro-optimising
check memory and I/O, not only CPU
keep the code readable; record the gain

name: security-review
description: Checks code and configuration for security problems. Use before releasing anything that handles input, secrets, auth or money.
must: untrusted input: validation, injection (SQL, shell, path), deserialisation
authn and authz on every entry point
secrets never in code, logs or errors
dependencies with known vulnerabilities
least privilege for files, users, network
report with severity, impact and fix

name: handle-errors-and-logging
description: Designs error handling and logs that make failures visible and diagnosable. Use when writing code that can fail.
must: fail loudly at the boundary; never swallow errors
errors carry context (what, which input)
log levels used consistently; structured logs
no secrets or personal data in logs
retries only for transient errors, with backoff and a limit

name: git-workflow
description: Commits, branches and pull requests done cleanly. Use for any version control work.
must: one logical change per commit; imperative subject under 72 chars
branch per change; pull request with what and why
never force-push shared branches; never commit secrets
rebase or merge per project convention
check git status and diff before committing

name: ci-cd
description: Sets up or fixes continuous integration and delivery. Use for GitHub Actions or other pipelines.
must: CI runs the same commands as local: lint, type check, tests, build
fast feedback: cache dependencies, fail fast
pin action versions; least-privilege tokens
deploy from main after green CI; easy rollback
read the failing step's log before changing anything

name: containers-and-deploy
description: Packages and deploys services with containers. Use for Dockerfiles, compose, Kubernetes or a server deploy.
must: small images: multi-stage builds, pinned base, non-root user
config from environment; secrets from a secret store
health checks and graceful shutdown
resource limits
a rollback plan for every deploy

name: dependencies
description: Adds, upgrades or removes dependencies safely. Use when changing what a project depends on.
must: prefer the standard library; justify each new dependency
check licence, maintenance and size
pin versions with a lockfile
upgrade one at a time and run the tests
read the changelog for breaking changes

name: observability
description: Makes a service observable: logs, metrics, traces, alerts. Use when running anything in production.
must: the four signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation
structured logs with a request id
traces across service boundaries
alerts on symptoms users feel, with a runbook link
dashboards that answer: is it working, is it fast

name: incident-response
description: Handles a production incident and writes the postmortem. Use when something is down or broken for users.
must: mitigate first (rollback, disable, scale), then find the cause
one person coordinates; keep a timeline
communicate status in plain words
blameless postmortem: impact, timeline, root cause, actions with owners
actions that prevent the class of failure

name: data-durability
description: Protects data: backups, restores, migrations without loss. Use when data must not be lost.
must: backups on another disk and off-site
restores tested on a schedule
consistent copies of live databases (backup API, snapshots)
writes fsynced where loss matters; atomic file replace
migrations reversible; backup before risky changes

name: write-docs
description: Writes documentation people use: README, how-to, reference. Use when documenting code or a project.
must: README: what it is, install, quick start, examples, limits
task-based how-to guides with copy-paste commands
plain words, short sentences, real examples
docs next to the code and updated with it
no marketing; state limitations

name: explain-code
description: Explains code clearly to another developer. Use when the user asks what code does or how it works.
must: start with the purpose in one sentence
inputs, outputs, side effects
how the parts connect; who calls it
what is easy to break
plain words; quote the lines that matter

name: data-analysis
description: Analyses a dataset correctly and reports what it shows. Use for questions answered from data files or databases.
must: look at the data first: shape, types, missing values, duplicates
state the question and the metric
check results with a second method or a sanity check
report numbers with their uncertainty and caveats
reproducible script, not manual steps

name: ml-experiment
description: Runs a machine-learning experiment that can be trusted. Use when training or evaluating models.
must: fixed train/validation/test split by the right unit; no leakage
a simple baseline first
the metric chosen before training
several seeds; report mean and spread
log config, data version and results
compare against the baseline honestly

name: research-and-compare
description: Researches options and compares them to recommend one. Use when choosing a library, tool, approach or vendor.
must: criteria first, weighted by what matters for this project
2-4 real options, including doing nothing
facts with sources; separate vendor claims from measurements
a table, then a recommendation with the reason
say what is not verified
